_comment: Per-token rates in US dollars per MILLION tokens, for bench/cost.py.
The Anthropic rows are not estimates. The opus-5 row was recovered by
least squares from the 11 turns in usage_events that carry
cost_basis='list' -- the CLI's own reported list price -- and it fits all
11 to the cent, worst absolute error $0.0000. It then matched the
published rate card exactly, which is what makes the derivation
trustworthy rather than a coincidence of round numbers.
The cache_write figures are the 1-hour TTL rate (2x base input), because
that is the one the fit recovered: $10.00/MTok against a $5.00 base. The
5-minute rate is 1.25x and is listed here for reference only.
Azure rows are deliberately ABSENT, not zero. Nobody has recorded what
this deployment pays for gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.4-mini,
gpt-5.4-mini-copilot or gpt-5-mini, and those names look like internal
deployment aliases rather than public SKUs, so no public rate card
applies to them. bench/cost.py reports an unrecorded rate as 'rate not
recorded' and never as free -- a model nobody priced must not come out
cheapest.
The vllm row is 0.0 because it is self-hosted: no marginal per-token
charge. Its cost is wall-clock and GPU occupancy, which the benchmark
records separately as total_s.
WARNING about usage_events: every non-Anthropic cost_usd in that table is
opus-5 list pricing applied to the wrong backend. Verified by recomputing
each model's recorded total at opus rates -- all four Azure models and
Qwen3.6 match to the cent. Only cost_basis='list' rows are real billing.
